batch_strategy: Family-conditioned response curves with late-tail repair, loading contrasts, and ordinary controls

choices.reason: The model predicts 21.70/42.51 ml for donor-containing m58 at 50/1. This high-strength point tests whether the broad phenolic tail seen in measured m58 behavior, including 0296d31e8c2e55602a19, transfers across loading amount.

The model predicts only 3.79/10.74 ml at 1/1, while measured m172 at 50/1 in 419f6eb4080dcb9d293b was 14.74/32.88 ml. This is a direct low-to-high strength transition probe for scaffold-specific solvent response.

The predicted 6.18/16.82 ml interval is broad for donor-free fused aromatic m4. It tests whether the late-tail correction transfers to hydrophobic halogenated chemistry, complementing the ordinary donor-free controls in H5.

This m176 1/1 point is predicted at 5.72/13.66 ml and supplies a lower-strength anchor for the halogenated benzophenone-like family. It can be compared with the measured 94bc3fc118d3761c7685 response.

The model predicts 4.00/9.80 ml for a high-loading m201 control. Comparing it with measured 801e2da4e098caa8fc7c tests whether loading and polarity corrections remain compact for donor-free nitro chemistry.

The model predicts 5.05/11.86 ml for low-strength multifunctional m178. This baseline helps locate the onset of the broad carbonyl-rich tail represented by measured late rows such as d2921349ba8d9cef15a4.
The model predicts 18.40/49.78 ml for m209 at 20/1. It fills the response curve between measured 2a7062ac85d66260b3be at weak strength, 534afc6bd39a8f7923d8 at 5/1, and 80f546c47198fa7c6dbf at 50/1.

This ordinary m93 ester control is predicted at 6.46/11.24 ml at 5/1 PE. It tests whether compact ester behavior stays centered while high-tail corrections are learned from multifunctional rows; measured b59d10badf9681a661a6 is a weak-strength reference.

The model predicts 4.19/9.50 ml for highly hydrophobic donor-free m0 at 50/1. It extends the donor-free control range beyond measured 002ce3d7c637632f0ebe and tests for overcorrection of ordinary hydrophobic rows.

This high-strength m3 control is predicted at 6.73/16.14 ml. It tests whether a polyaryl donor-free scaffold develops a tail distinct from the broad heteroatom-rich failures, using measured 8a7e4cadaea654017cb4 as a neighboring reference.

The model predicts 6.92/14.89 ml for m212 at 0/1 PE with substantial loading. This complements measured 18a189c89f59ac1d5a9f and tests whether amine-containing diaryl behavior changes with loading solvent and solvent system.
The predicted 10.01/24.73 ml baseline for m141 at 1/1 provides a local anchor before the severe late behavior measured at 5/1 in 65f4f125b5e1f8137bd9 and at 10/1 in 7fb4f90753d40dd25be0.

The model predicts 16.73/34.11 ml for m198 at 10/1 and high loading. This probes whether the nitro-aldehyde family follows the broad late response seen in measured 8ab554cd154e9749790b and 163874b97308a1ea2507.

This m23 ester control is predicted at 4.12/8.55 ml at 1/1 PE. It anchors compact ordinary chemistry against the unusually broad predicted and measured tails elsewhere, complementing measured fae79bab43155a52988f and 90ae8e9fe447f6a79598.

The predicted 8.59/19.48 ml point for m185 tests a halogenated aldehyde family with possible donor-free late behavior. It provides a local structural comparison for H4 without assuming that all aldehydes share one transition location.
The model predicts 9.81/23.62 ml for m194 at 2/1. This is a useful finish-tail probe for a fused aldehyde scaffold and can discriminate local tail behavior from the compact ordinary rows.
The predicted 5.82/9.51 ml m73 point is an intermediate-strength aromatic ester control. It tests whether the model's central V1/V2 calibration remains stable outside the late-retention families.
The second m176 point is predicted at 6.48/12.49 ml at 2/1, forming a same-molecule strength contrast with a54f1c9df0f04b361e55. Together they can estimate a local onset and finish slope.

The model predicts 6.68/11.55 ml for high-strength m126. This compact anisole control tests whether strength-related corrections learned from late aromatic families leak into ordinary donor-free ether chemistry.

The model predicts 6.41/14.86 ml for m131 at 5/1. This fills the transition between measured low-strength m131 behavior in fb65053351114fb51265 and the overpredicted high-strength point c060c367e4e5bf6955cb.

The predicted 4.82/11.10 ml m8 point probes a sulfur-containing heteroaromatic scaffold at intermediate strength. It tests whether heteroatom identity, rather than generic aromaticity, controls the finish tail.

This low-strength m125 anchor is predicted at 6.29/11.99 ml. It is needed to interpret the much broader high-strength m125 candidate and to separate a real response transition from a global tail correction.

The model predicts 39.31/73.94 ml for m125 at 5/1, making this a direct V2-tail repair probe. It complements measured broad m125 behavior in 5c2bc1d92128a17d996d, c4b5a5499258f39b7ac1, and 03744855d469f4cca7e6.

The model predicts 15.40/19.66 ml for m96 at 10/1. This tests the intermediate part of a strongly nonlinear response curve between measured compact 5/1 behavior in a3c817ff559d5c946cc8 and the high-strength result in 5bad82a6cffd60e7a6c9.
The predicted 22.52/30.99 ml m96 point at 20/1 probes whether onset and finish rise together at stronger solvent conditions. It provides a second local anchor for direct V2-tail calibration.

The model predicts 6.57/62.53 ml for m177 at 50/1 and low volume. This isolates whether the very long finish measured in b514312eda7950cdcf1c persists when loading volume is reduced, relative to 27bac953781c17a3a74b.

This m160 point is predicted at 7.40/19.09 ml at 1/1 and high loading. It provides a low-strength loading anchor for the measured severe donor/acceptor-rich behavior in ad833f34f6b91872362d and b21061720e23b7a5bdcb.

The model predicts 4.85/10.95 ml for low-strength m159. This baseline is essential for separating the ordinary response from the extreme measured high-strength tail in a17bcdddcf0799baeee2 and the intermediate behavior in d3d2b36ec3417c1c1c6c.

The predicted 6.91/17.86 ml m146 point at 0/1 tests the low-strength baseline of a severe heteroaromatic family. It helps localize the transition seen in measured 9e3ce3497298084abd83, 23ef03f3e75e40b20095, and 61b73b8065ae2ece22eb.

The model predicts 6.42/14.74 ml for low-strength m118. This is a high-value baseline because measured m118 responses range from compact behavior in 2cc254396123c76b9a13 to very late behavior in 2d178efe0181baca2bd5 and 24a9086a8e2c8015c232.
The predicted 7.46/11.83 ml m123 point at 2/1 supplies a compact condition anchor for a family that includes the broad measured high-strength response c6159dcb5802e62284d1.

The model predicts 7.26/16.95 ml for low-strength m28. This probes the onset of the strongly delayed carbonyl response measured across 351c17dfa8f46a8cb40a, 0dccaa29989ef4956786, db7f9ffa50eb931613f6, and 0d18f3f10c8377d12316.

hypotheses.content: Solvent-strength response and onset/finish coupling remain scaffold-specific, with transition locations and slopes that cannot be represented reliably by a global PE/EA trend.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Same-molecule and same-family condition contrasts can teach local transition boundaries and slopes for V1 and V2 instead of imposing one global solvent-strength correction.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do transition locations transfer within functional-group families, or must they remain scaffold-specific?

hypotheses.content: Loading amount and loading-solvent volume alter V1 and V2 differently across scaffolds, so mass alone is insufficient as a universal loading correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Loading contrasts can separate sample-loading effects from mobile-phase effects and improve direct V2-tail learning.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At fixed molecule and PE/EA ratio, does loading primarily shift onset, expand finish, or change both in a scaffold-dependent way?

hypotheses.content: V2 and interval width require direct local calibration; predicted quantile width is useful for finding probes but is not a generally calibrated estimate of finish-tail behavior.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Direct finish labels in broad and compact predicted regimes can teach retraining when a wide interval reflects a real tail.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Can structural descriptors predict finish width across families, or are local scaffold-condition anchors required?

hypotheses.content: Late-retention failures cluster across heteroatom-rich, carbonyl-rich, heteroaromatic, and multifunctional scaffolds, but their transition locations remain local.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Related but distinct late-retention families need local anchors so the model can learn transferable structural signals without merging their transition locations.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which local structural environments best identify a scaffold's transition into late V2 behavior?

hypotheses.content: Novelty alone is insufficient; donor-free, halogenated, and compact acceptor-only controls are needed to constrain overcorrection of ordinary rows.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Ordinary controls protect overall Row-distribution accuracy while local tail repairs are learned.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: After tail repair, do ordinary donor-free and compact acceptor-only rows remain centered across strength and loading regimes?

hypotheses.content: Severe late rows form distinct scaffold-specific response families, so a correction learned from one delayed aromatic or multifunctional scaffold should not be transferred indiscriminately to another.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The batch samples several local late-response families so retraining can learn family-conditioned residual structure rather than one global tail shift.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which scaffold descriptors or interaction environments predict membership in each late-retention response family?

feedback_interpretation: Recent measurements strengthened the case for local response curves and family-specific tail behavior. The measured m172 point 419f6eb4080dcb9d293b was far later than its lower-strength model expectation, while m131 points c060c367e4e5bf6955cb and fb65053351114fb51265 showed that the same scaffold can shift from severe model overprediction to near-centered behavior across conditions. The measured m96 result a3c817ff559d5c946cc8 remained compact despite a broad prediction, reinforcing that quantile width is not a calibrated tail probability. The long m177 finish in b514312eda7950cdcf1c and the extreme m159 result a17bcdddcf0799baeee2 continue to support direct V2-tail repair, but they also argue against transferring one correction globally.
batch_rationale: The batch combines local strength curves for m172, m176, m125, m96, m177, m159, m118, and m131 with loading or solvent-system contrasts for m58, m209, m212, m160, and m201. High predicted-tail candidates target unresolved V2 failures, while low-strength anchors determine whether those tails turn on locally or reflect broad model bias. Donor-free hydrophobic controls m0 and m3, compact ester and ether controls m23, m93, m126, m8, and m73, and other ordinary controls constrain overcorrection of the central Row-distribution. The selected families span carbonyl, heteroaromatic, aldehyde, ester, donor-containing, donor-free, and multifunctional chemistry, so retraining can learn structure-condition interactions and scaffold-specific residuals across both ordinary and failure regions.
